plant_tasks.text: Elwood Energy was sold in two pieces. Hull Street Energy bought units 1 to 4, 8 and 9 in 2025 (units 8 and 9 retired June 1, 2025 and are already retired in GEM). Utility Dive reported in April 2026 that Hull Street would retire units 1 to 4 (600 MW) by June 1, 2026, and the August 2026 EIA-860M table lists plant 69979 'MPH Elwood' with GT1 to GT4 retired in 2026. Confirm with PJM's deactivation page (pjm.com/planning/service-requests/gen-deactivations/generator-deactivation-notices, letters named elwood-deactivation-extension.pdf and elwood-revision-8-9.pdf) whether GT1 to GT4 actually retired on June 1, 2026. If confirmed by the PJM letter and a second publisher, stage Status retired and Retired year 2026 for GT1 to GT4. If only one source, stage it as a single-source status change and say so.

Dairyland Power Cooperative bought Elwood units 5 to 7 on March 6, 2026 and withdrew their retirement notice on May 6, 2026 (PJM letter elwood-deactivation-withdraw-letter.pdf). Stage Owner(s) for GT5 to GT7 as Dairyland Power Cooperative [100%] if the closing is documented, and Owner(s) for GT1 to GT4 as Hull Street Energy's entity if that closing is documented. Run entity_lookup.py for both names before staging. Do not change the owner of GT8 and GT9 unless a source gives it.
Add a Status Detail line at the top for each unit group describing the 2024 to 2026 retirement notices and the withdrawal for units 5 to 7, with the PJM letter link in the text.

EIA-860M now lists the Hull Street units under a new plant code 69979 (MPH Elwood) while the original code 55199 stays with units 5 to 7. Say in a question which units carry which code; do not stage the ID columns.
